title: Vertical Intel Funnel & Hypothesis Lab — model landscape tracking and competitive signalization
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Build an operational 'Vertical Intel Funnel' and accompanying Hypothesis Lab to turn heterogeneous model signals into prioritized, action-ready recommendations for product, sales, and provisioning.

Background: We need a repeatable way to detect emergent model capability changes (latency/economics/feature parity) that matter to specific buyer verticals (finserv, legal, SaaS). Existing trackers are model-centric; this ticket flips the view to buyer friction -> signal mapping so PM and GTM can act faster.

Scope:
- Define funnel stages from raw signal ingestion (telemetry, third-party LLM releases, partner notes, public benchmarks) -> normalized signal events -> hypothesis formation -> probe cohort experiments -> action (model onboarding, routing rule changes, pricing adjustments).
- Design signal weighting for vertical relevance and operational cost (latency sensitivity, quantization tolerance, security requirements).
- Create a Hypothesis Lab template for rapid experiments (probe configs, success metrics, rollback thresholds).
- Deliver a lightweight dashboard and a set of alerting rules that feed into the incident/ops backlog and sales enablement doc.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- We value speed of detection over perfect accuracy in early funnels; false positives will be triaged by an analyst step.
- Avoid building heavy ML classifiers in Phase 1; rely on rule-based scoring + human-in-the-loop verification.
- Must respect PII/security constraints when using customer telemetry; use aggregated signals only for early phases.

Deliverables:
1) Signal schema and mapping doc (vertical attributes, confidence bands, canonical event types).
2) Hypothesis Lab templates + experiment runbook.
3) Dashboard prototype with vertical filters and signal heatmap.
4) Alerting rules and playbook for ops/SE to act on high-confidence signals.

Success criteria: actionable lists that reduce time-to-decision for model fallback or procurement by 30% in pilot verticals.
